sense: a sight, what is happening before one’s eyes

terms.comment: Anything that is there to be seen, a sad sight as much as a fine one; also a public show, games or a play (see performance).

terms.gloss: the look, the appearance of a thing
evidence: Sall. C. 31.1: immūtāta faciēs urbis erat (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The look of a place, how things stand there: in Sallust, the whole scene in the city had changed. First of all a face, then the form and look of anything (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Ō spectāculum illud nōn modo hominibus sed undīs ipsīs et lītoribus lūctuōsum!
phrases.english: Oh, that scene, a grief not only to men but to the very waves and shores!

phrases.latin: nōn hoc ista sibi tempus spectācula poscit
phrases.english: this is no time for looking at the sights

sources: Lewis & Short: spectaculum · Lewis & Short: facies
